identity.title: Representation Preserving Multiclass Agnostic to Realizable Reduction

scoped_summary: False partial-class extension under explicit definitions and invalid representation-cost lower-bound inference; total-predictor reduction not refuted.

problems.title: Zero-loss abstention invalidates partial reduction
problems.claim: Theorem B.3 converts any realizable partial learner into agnostic partial learner
problems.location: PDF pp10-12, Definitions B.1-B.2, Theorem B.3, Eqs14-15
problems.assumptions: Finite X=Y=A={0,1}; star-loss0; c0=(0,star), c1=(star,0); H={h0=(0,0)}; full finite sigma algebras; only realizable D are delta(0,0),delta(1,0)
problems.check: Constant h0 is perfect on both realizable D. For D=delta(0,1), min empirical partial loss=0 for every n, hence comparator0, but only H predictor has risk1. At eps1/2,delta1/4 success probability0.
problems.result: False theorem under stated definitions; zero loss does not entail required support.
problems.counterevidence: Changing star loss or restricting comparator changes definitions; total predictor Theorem4.1 not refuted
problems.impact: Core partial extension and dependent guarantees

problems.title: Lower-bound example does not isolate representation cost
problems.claim: Section6 says extra 1/epsilon is unavoidable due to representation preservation; Theorem6.1 displays MRE/MAG=Omega(epsilon^-2)
problems.assumptions: Same total-predictor instance; theorem's n1,m2 constant-class example; fixed nontrivial confidence
problems.check: MRE<=MAG. Reversing ratio still leaves H equal entire predictor space. Empirical majority in H needs at most 2 epsilon^-2 log(1/delta) samples.
problems.result: Displayed ratio impossible and corrected-direction example does not demonstrate representation-specific extra factor
problems.counterevidence: Ratio may be typo; a different construction may prove representation penalty, and upper-bound algorithm survives
problems.impact: Stated theoretical optimality rationale, not whole reduction
problems.correction: Only noise-sampling interpretation supported; no replacement optimality theorem
